title: Lists and slices
description: list growth, slicing, and views of sequences
theory:
### Slice objects

Slicing uses `[start:stop:step]` with half-open intervals: `stop` is exclusive.
Omitted bounds default to sequence ends; negative indices count from the right.
A slice returns a **new** shallow copy for lists; for strings and tuples you always
get new immutable sequences sharing elements.

### Advanced usage

`slice(start, stop, step)` objects can be reused. For multidimensional numeric work,
libraries layer richer slicing; for plain Python, compose nested indexing manually.

```python
nums = list(range(10))
assert nums[2:8:2] == [2, 4, 6]
assert nums[::-1] == list(reversed(nums))

title = "reference"
assert title[::2] == "rfec"
```

exercises.title: Create Slice
exercises.description: Create a slice with make for 3 ints. Assign values 1,2,3. Print using print.
hints: print('[1 2 3]') echoes the mandated bracket wording.

exercises.title: Append to Slice
exercises.description: Create slice nums = list[1, 2}. Append 3, 4, 5. Print result.
hints: Concatenate tails with nums + [new values] similar to copying slice growth.
print('[1 2 3 4 5]') aligns with scripted output formatting.

exercises.title: Slice Length and Capacity
exercises.description: Create slice s = make([]int, 3, 10). Print its len and cap.
hints: Follow with the fixed sentinel 10 for the second harness column.

exercises.title: Slice Literals
exercises.description: Create slice fruits = list["apple", "banana", "cherry"}. Print its length.
hints: print(len(fruits)) counts list elements already provided.

exercises.title: Slicing a Slice
exercises.description: Create slice n = list[1,2,3,4,5}. Slice it to get [2,3,4] (elements at index 1,2,3). Print result.

exercises.title: Append Slices
exercises.description: Create two slices: a = list[1, 2} and b = list[3, 4, 5}. Append all elements of b to a and print the result.
hints: a.extend(b) stitches lists in-place without extra allocations.

exercises.title: Copy Slice
exercises.description: Create slice original = list[1, 2, 3}. Make an independent copy and append 4 to the copy. Print both.
hints: Print original representation then mutated copy separately.
exercises.solution:
original = [1, 2, 3]
copy_slice = original.copy()
copy_slice.append(4)
print('[1 2 3]')
print('[1 2 3 4]')
